column3: The Hebrew describes responsibility for song with the word hands; BSB expresses this as charge of the music.
The Hebrew says they stood at their service according to their regulation; BSB says they performed duties according to regulations given them, without a separate giving verb in Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes these men as standing; BSB interprets this as serving.
The Hebrew calls Asaph his brother and describes him as standing; BSB names Heman, uses kinsman, and interprets standing as serving.
The Hebrew calls the fellow Levites their brothers; BSB uses fellow Levites.
The Hebrew begins with Aaron and his sons making smoke on the two altars, then speaks of all the Most Holy Place’s work; BSB places the general work first and describes presenting offerings.
The Hebrew calls these the sons of Aaron; BSB uses descendants.
The Hebrew speaks of settlements according to their encampments within their territory and says the lot was theirs; BSB speaks of assigned territories and specifies the first lot.
The Hebrew uses active plural giving agents; BSB expresses the gift passively.
The Hebrew uses active plural giving agents and singular field of the city; BSB expresses the gift passively and uses plural fields.

The Hebrew uses active plural giving agents and plural cities of refuge, and names pasturelands with Libnah and Eshtemoa; BSB uses a passive, calls Hebron a city of refuge, and defers the pasturelands to verse 59.
The Hebrew names each city’s pasturelands here; BSB lists only the city names in this verse.
The Hebrew names Ashan and Beth-shemesh with their pasturelands; BSB additionally includes Juttah.
The Hebrew names Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth; BSB additionally includes Gibeon. The Hebrew separately repeats pasturelands for each named city.
